(CoinDesk) Summary * Gemini and Apex signed a letter of intent to distribute crypto prediction-market contracts to brokerage clients. * Gemini would provide execution and clearing, giving brokers access without requiring them to build direct exchange infrastructure. * The deal builds on the New York-based firm’s push into regulated prediction markets after securing key CFTC exchange and clearing licenses. Gemini (GEMI), the cryptocurrency platform founded by the billionaire Winklevoss twins, is teaming up with Apex Fintech Solutions to expand distribution of its regulated crypto prediction markets to brokerage firms, the companies said in a Monday announcement. Under a letter of intent, subsidiary Gemini Titan would become the exclusive regulated venue for crypto event contracts distributed through Apex’s futures commission merchant (FCM) to its brokerage customers. An FCM is a regulated firm that handles customer orders and funds for trading futures and other derivatives. Gemini would handle execution and clearing, allowing brokerages using Apex to offer crypto-based event contracts without having to build their own connections to a prediction-market exchange. summary: Title: Live updates: Bitcoin moves closer to $80,000, but rally could bring profit taking URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/08/24/live-updates-bitcoin-holds-usd77-000-as-xrp-zcash-pull-back-after-a-big-weekly-rally Published Time: 2026-08-24T08:05:57.101Z Markdown Content: coverage ended Aug 24, 2026, 9:00 PM ## Live updates: Bitcoin retreats after nearing $80,000, with analysts eyeing breather after big run With bond yields still near multi-year highs, focus turns to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's upcoming Jackson Hole address. ![Image 1: Helene Braun](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F4d1961b17d266e7c19bdcc14478d59b99ee0a3fc-944x554.png%3Fw%3D64%26h%3D64%26fit%3Dcrop%26crop%3Dfocalpoint%26auto%3Dformat&w=96&q=75) ## Bitcoin’s next move hinges on spot buying, says Charles Schwab's Jim Ferraioli Bitcoin may need a new source of buying to extend its rally after $6.4 billion in leveraged short perpetual futures positions were liquidated since Wednesday, according to Charles Schwab’s Jim Ferraioli. “Ultimately, short squeezes tend to be short lived, but this could settle the debate as to whether the bottom is in,” said Ferraioli, head of crypto research and strategy. One place to watch next is the futures market. Bitcoin futures are now in backwardation, a relatively rare setup where futures prices sit below spot. Ferraioli said hedge funds that appear bullish because they are net long futures may instead be repositioning basis trades rather than betting on bitcoin’s direction. That could change if the futures curve returns to contango, its more common state. As cash-and-carry traders unwind positions that are currently long futures and short spot, they would need to buy bitcoin in the spot market, which could help support bitcoin after the short squeeze fades. * * * ![Image 2: Helene Braun](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vc

Ethereum lending platform Term Finance has lost an estimated $8.5 million after an attacker seemingly acquired enough voting power to take control of some of its lending vaults.
